title: Multiplicativity of fibrewise algebraically trivial rigidified line modules
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $A\to S$ be a proper smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose geometric fibres are smooth proper geometrically connected group schemes. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; smoothness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. A line module is an $\mathcal O$-module on the small etale site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $T$ be any $S$-scheme and let $M$ be a line module on $A_T=A\times_ST$, with a rigidification $r:e_T^*M\simeq\mathcal O_T$ at the identity section. Suppose that on each geometric fibre $M$ is algebraically equivalent to the trivial module: the equivalence relation is generated by pairs of fibres of a line-module family over a connected smooth parameter variety. Let $m:A_T\times_TA_T\to A_T$ be addition and $p_1,p_2$ its two projections. There exists an isomorphism $m^*M\simeq p_1^*M\otimes p_2^*M$. This assertion includes nonreduced and non-Noetherian parameter schemes $T$; it asserts no existence of a lift to a thickening of $T$.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4(c), printed p.36, field multiplicativity criterion. Relative algebraic-space and arbitrary-parameter version is an agent-stated prerequisite; it is not asserted to be proved by the field proposition. Relative theorem-of-cube and Picard-kernel input: Mumford--Fogarty--Kirwan, Geometric Invariant Theory, Chapter 6, section 2 (WANTED).

proof.text: Write $f:A\to S$ and $e:S\to A$. Smoothness on etale scheme charts implies flatness by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Each geometric fibre is a proper smooth connected group scheme, so [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] makes it geometrically integral. This verifies geometrically integral fibres also over residue fields: for any extension $K/\kappa(s)$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $K$; the surjective faithfully flat base change $A_\Omega\to A_K$ descends reducedness on etale charts, and its irreducible source has irreducible image. Thus $A_K$ is integral. The locally Noetherian base, properness, finite presentation and section required by [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] are now all present. Obtain its separated commutative group algebraic space $P\to S$, locally of finite presentation, classifying all identity-rigidified line modules. For every scheme $U\to S$ its canonical map $\mathcal O_U\to(f_U)_*\mathcal O_{A_U}$ is an isomorphism. Use the full Picard space, without asserting smoothness or properness of its neutral component.

source.place: Tags 0D28, 0D2B, 0D2C (rigidified Picard representation); spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0E0S (universal functions).

proof.text: On any scheme the equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison] lets us regard an etale line module as an ordinary invertible module, and identifies the trivial objects and their isomorphisms. The comparison with the tensor, dual and arbitrary morphism pullbacks used below can be checked on frames: if transition units are $g_{ij}$, the tensor, dual and pullback transition units are respectively $g_{ij}h_{ij}$, $g_{ij}^{-1}$ and the images of $g_{ij}$ in the pulled-back structure sheaf. These are the same formulas on both sites. The resulting local comparisons agree on overlaps and glue. We may therefore apply the scheme theorem of the cube to the geometric-fibre line modules and their parameter families.

source.place: Invertible-module descent and the ordinary/etale equivalence; explicit frame calculation for the operations.

proof.text:
For a commutative group space $C\to U$ with identity $e_C$ and a line module $L$ on $C$, put
$$N(L)=m_C^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*L^{-1}\otimes q^*e_C^*L,$$
where $q:C\times_UC\to U$ and $L^{-1}$ is the dual line module. Both identity-axis restrictions are canonically trivial: on $(e_C,y)$ the four factors are $L_y,L_e^{-1},L_y^{-1},L_e$, and on $(x,e_C)$ they are $L_x,L_x^{-1},L_e^{-1},L_e$. Evaluation cancels these pairs, and the two cancellations agree at $(e_C,e_C)$. Tensor products, duals and pullbacks in this formula commute with base change, so $N(L)$ and its axis trivializations do too. Isomorphic line modules give isomorphic normalized differences, and $N(\mathcal O_C)$ is trivial.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4(c), printed p.36; identity normalization written explicitly.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed geometric residue field $\Omega$ of $T$, and put $B=A_\Omega$. By Step 1, $B$ is a proper geometrically integral scheme with rational point $e$. Consider one generating pair for algebraic equivalence, given by a line-module family $F$ on $B\times_\Omega Z$, with $Z$ a connected smooth parameter variety and endpoints $z_0,z_1\in Z(\Omega)$. Apply Step 3 over $Z$: the line module $N(F)$ on $B\times_\Omega B\times_\Omega Z$ is trivial on $e\times B\times Z$ and $B\times e\times Z$. If $N(F_{z_0})$ is trivial, [lem-sc-general-theorem-of-cube], with $X=Y=B$, $x=y=e$ and parameter $Z$, makes $N(F)$ trivial, hence makes $N(F_{z_1})$ trivial. Exchanging $z_0,z_1$ proves the reverse implication. Starting with $N(\mathcal O_B)$ and following the finite chain that defines algebraic equivalence, we obtain $N(M_\Omega)\simeq\mathcal O_{B\times B}$. Thus the entire normalized difference, rather than just its pointwise fibres, is trivial over every geometric fibre of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0BF4, theorem-of-the-cube; applied to the generating families of algebraic equivalence.

proof.text: Return to arbitrary $T$ and set $C=A_T$. Regard $N(M)$ as a family of line modules on the first copy of $C$, with second copy $C$ as parameter and the first-axis trivialization of Step 3 as rigidification. The classification for algebraic-space parameters and arbitrary scheme base change in [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] gives a $T$-morphism $h:C\to P_T$. The second-axis trivialization, compatible at the intersection, gives $h e_T=0$. Step 4 and the same classification give $h_\Omega=0$ as a morphism for every geometric point of $T$: to respect the parameterwise rigidification, multiply any trivialization of $N(M_\Omega)$ by the inverse of its value on $e\times B$, pulled back from the parameter $B$. This makes that value $1$, so the rigidified family represents the zero map. No dual abelian space or infinitesimal lifting theorem has been used.

source.place: Tags 0D28 and 0D2B, normalization at the section and classification of rigidified families.

proof.text:
The map $p:C=A_T\to T$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The target $P_T\to T$ is separated: its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $P\to S$. On each affine test, pulling back a closed immersion defined by $I$ gives the closed immersion defined by the extended ideal, since $(R/I)\otimes_RR'=R'/IR'$. It is also locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] applied to $P\to S$. At every $t\in T$, Step 5 says that the image of $h$ on an algebraically closed residue-field fibre is the single identity point. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-space-finite-image-neighbourhood] to $h$ at $t$. It supplies an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq T$ and a factorization
$$C_V\xrightarrow{a}Z\xrightarrow{j}P_V$$
of $h_V$, where $Z$ is an affine scheme finite over $V$ and $j$ is a closed immersion. These neighbourhoods cover $T$; neither $T$ nor $V$ has been assumed Noetherian or reduced.

On each $V$ let $p_V:C_V\to V$ and $s=e_V:V\to C_V$. The canonical functions assertion of [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard] says that $p_V^\sharp:\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\Gamma(C_V,\mathcal O)$ is an isomorphism. Since $p_Vs=1$, its inverse is $s^\sharp$. Put $b=as:V\to Z$. Then
$$(bp_V)^\sharp=p_V^\sharp s^\sharp a^\sharp=a^\sharp.$$
The affine-target bijection of [lem-sfb-space-affine-target-global-functions] applies to the algebraic space $C_V$ and affine scheme $Z$, and its injectivity gives $a=bp_V$. Hence $h_V=jbp_V=(h_Vs)p_V=0$, using $he_T=0$. This calculation uses the actual structure rings, including their nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 05Z1, lemma-morphism-to-affine-scheme; combine with universal functions from spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0E0S.

proof.text: The equalities $h_V=0$ on the open cover of $T$ give $h=0$: on every scheme test of $C$, restrict to the inverse images of the $V$ and use the sheaf uniqueness for $P_T$ in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By the algebraic-space-parameter classification of [lem-sfb-rigidified-space-picard], the family $N(M)$ is therefore isomorphic to the trivial rigidified family on $C\times_TC$. The given rigidification $r:e_T^*M\simeq\mathcal O_T$ trivializes the last factor $q^*e_T^*M$ in Step 3. Tensor the resulting trivialization by $p_1^*M\otimes p_2^*M$ and cancel each dual pair to obtain $m^*M\simeq p_1^*M\otimes p_2^*M$. This proves the statement for the originally given arbitrary $T$.

source.place: Tag 0D28, rigidified class zero and the explicit tensor cancellation.
